A_target.statement:
Let $R \subseteq \R^2$ be a region with [[Definition:Piecewise Smooth Curve|piecewise smooth]] boundary.
Let $P_n$ be inscribed [[Definition:Polygon|polygons]] whose vertices on $\partial R$ have maximum spacing tending to $0$.
Then:
:$\map {\operatorname {Area} } R = \displaystyle \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {\operatorname {Area} } {P_n}$

B_source.statement:
Let $P$ be a [[Definition:Simple Polygon|simple polygon]] and $\set {T_i}$ any [[Definition:Triangulation|triangulation]] of $P$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \map {\operatorname {Area} } P = \sum_i \map {\operatorname {Area} } {T_i}$

substitutions.the polygon P: a sequence of inscribed polygons with vertices dense in the boundary
substitutions.the additive sum of triangle areas: the integral of the area element

derived.the limiting sum of triangle areas: the area of the curved region

validity_conditions: the boundary curve must be rectifiable so that inscribed polygons converge in area
the region must be simply connected for a single triangulation argument to apply directly
proof_plan: Choose points $p_1, \ldots, p_n$ in order on $\partial R$ and join them to form the inscribed polygon $P_n$.

Triangulate $P_n$ and sum the triangle areas.
For a triangle with vertices $a, b, c$:
:$\map {\operatorname {Area} } T = \dfrac 1 2 \size {\map \det {b - a, c - a} }$
Refine the vertex set so that the maximum edge length tends to $0$.

If $R$ is [[Definition:Convex Set (Vector Space)|convex]], adding vertices increases $\map {\operatorname {Area} } {P_n}$, which is bounded by $\map {\operatorname {Area} } R$, so the sequence converges by the [[Monotone Convergence Theorem (Real Analysis)|Monotone Convergence Theorem]].
In general, $R \symdif P_n$ lies within a strip around $\partial R$ of width $\to 0$, whose area tends to $0$ by [[Definition:Rectifiable Curve|rectifiability]].
